Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and may Allah send blessings and peace upon our Prophet Muhammad, and upon his family and companions, and those who follow them in goodness until the Day of Judgment.

To proceed: this is the weekly session called the "Open Door" meeting, and it is the ninety-ninth. This session takes place on Thursday, the fourteenth of Rabi' al-Awwal in the year one thousand four hundred and sixteen (AH), and in it we speak, by the will of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, about the tafsir of Surat al-'Asr.

Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿By time, indeed mankind is in loss﴾ [al-'Asr 1-2]. So what is meant by al-'Asr?

It has been said: the intended meaning of al-'Asr is the end of the day, because the end of the day is its best part; and the 'Asr prayer is called the middle prayer (al-Salat al-Wusta), i.e., the most excellent (al-Fudla), as the Prophet (ﷺ) named it.

And it has been said: al-'Asr is time itself. This is the more correct view: al-'Asr is time, which Allah swore by because of what occurs within it of changing circumstances, shifting affairs, and the alternation of days among people, and other things that are witnessed in the present and reported about in the past. So al-'Asr is the time in which creation lives, and its periods vary in hardship and ease, war and peace, health and sickness, righteous deeds and evil deeds, and other things that are known to all.

On what did Allah swear? On His saying: ﴿indeed mankind is in loss﴾. The word "mankind" (al-Insan) here is general, because the intended meaning is the genus. The sign of a noun intended in a general sense is that the word "kull" (all) can take its place, i.e., in place of (al-, the definite article). So here, if it were said, "Every human is in loss," that would be the meaning.

The meaning of the noble verse is that Allah swore an oath concerning the condition of mankind, that they are in loss, i.e., in ruin and deficiency in all their circumstances, in this world and in the Hereafter, except for those whom Allah, Mighty and Majestic, excepts. And this sentence, as you see, is emphasized with three emphases: the first is the oath; the second is "inna"; the third is the lam. And He used the phrase ﴿in loss﴾ so that it would be more emphatic than saying "losers" (lakhasir). That is because "fi" (in) — what does it mean? It means enclosure, so it is as if the human being is immersed in loss, and loss surrounds him from every side.

﴿Except those who believed and did righteous deeds and advised one another to truth and advised one another to patience﴾ [al-'Asr 3]. Allah, glorified and exalted, excepted those who possess these four attributes. The first attribute: faith that is not mixed with doubt or hesitation. In what? In what the Messenger (ﷺ) explained when Jibril asked him about faith; he said: "That you believe in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Last Day, and that you believe in divine decree, its good and its evil."[[Recorded by Muslim (8/1) from the hadith of Ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both.]] The explanation of this hadith would be lengthy if we discussed it now, but we have discussed it in many places. Those who believe in these six foundations are the believers, but it must be a faith with no doubt or hesitation; meaning that you believe in these things as though you see them with your own eyes.

People in this regard are of three categories:
The first category: a believer who is sincere, with faith that has no doubt or hesitation in it.
The second category: a disbelieving, denying rejecter.
The third category: the wavering one.

So who is saved from these three categories? The saved one is the first category, who believes with faith free of hesitation: he believes in Allah — in His existence, His names, His attributes, His divinity and His lordship, and other things known of the attributes of the Lord, Majestic and Exalted. He believes in the angels, who are an unseen world, whom Allah created from light, and assigned to tasks, some of which are known and some of which are not known. Jibril, peace be upon him, is charged with revelation, which he brings down from Allah to the prophets and messengers; Mikail is charged with rain and plants — i.e., Allah entrusted him with rain and all that relates to rain, and with plants; Israfil is charged with blowing the Trumpet; Malik is charged with the Fire; Ridwan is charged with Paradise. Among the angels are those whose names we do not know and whose tasks we also do not know. But it has come in a hadith from the Prophet (ﷺ) that "there is no spot of four fingers' breadth in the heavens except that there is an angel standing for Allah, or bowing, or prostrating"[[Recorded by al-Tirmidhi (2312) from the hadith of Abu Dharr, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I see what you do not see and hear what you do not hear. The heaven has creaked, and it has the right to creak; there is no spot of four fingers in it except that an angel is placing his forehead in prostration to Allah. By Allah, if you knew what I know, you would laugh little and weep much, and you would not enjoy women on beds, and you would go out to the high ground supplicating to Allah." I wish I had been a tree that is cut down. The phrase "I wish I had been a tree that is cut down" is the words of Abu Dharr, may Allah be pleased with him; see Musnad Ahmad (21516).]].

Likewise we believe in the books that Allah sent down to the messengers, peace be upon them, and we believe in the messengers. Those whom Allah has related to us, we believe in them by their individual identities; and those whom He has not related to us, we believe in them in general, because Allah has not related to us all the accounts of the messengers. Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿Among them are those We have related to you, and among them are those We have not related to you﴾ [Ghafir 78].

The Last Day is the Day of Resurrection, the day when people come out of their graves for recompense, "barefoot, naked, uncircumcised, and destitute"[[Recorded by al-Bukhari (3349) and Muslim (2860/58), the wording of the latter, with their two chains, from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood among us giving a sermon and said: "O people, you will be gathered to Allah barefoot, naked, uncircumcised: ﴿As We began the first creation, We will repeat it; a promise upon Us; indeed We are ever doing﴾ [al-Anbiya' 104] ..." The hadith. As for the word "destitute" (buhman), it came in what Ahmad (16042) recorded from the hadith of 'Abdullah ibn Unays, may Allah be pleased with him, in which it says: "People will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection — or he said: the servants — naked, uncircumcised, destitute."]]. "Barefoot" means those who have no sandals or shoes, i.e., their feet are bare; "naked" means those who have no clothes; "uncircumcised" means those who have not been circumcised; and "destitute" means those who have no wealth. They will be gathered in this state. "When the Prophet (ﷺ) mentioned that they would be naked, 'A'isha said: O Messenger of Allah, do men and women look at one another?! He said: 'The matter is greater than that'"[[Recorded by al-Bukhari (6527) and Muslim (2859/56), the wording of the latter, with their two chains, to 'A'isha who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "People will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection barefoot, naked, uncircumcised." I said: O Messenger of Allah, do men and women look at one another all together? He (ﷺ) said: "O 'A'isha, the matter is more severe than that they look at one another." As for the word "destitute" (buhman), it came in what Ahmad (16042) recorded from the hadith of 'Abdullah ibn Unays, may Allah be pleased with him, in which it says: "People will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection — or he said: the servants — naked, uncircumcised, destitute."]]; i.e., the matter is too great for them to look at one another, because each person is preoccupied with himself.

Shaykh al-Islam, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Among faith in the Last Day is belief in everything the Prophet (ﷺ) informed about that will occur after death. So it is obligatory to believe in the trial of the grave, i.e., the testing that the deceased undergoes when he is buried and his companions have turned away from him; two angels come to him and ask him about his Lord, his religion, and his Prophet[[Recorded by Abu Dawud (4753) with his chain from al-Bara' ibn 'Azib who said: We went out with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to the funeral of a man from the Ansar, and we reached the grave before it had been dug in its niche. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sat down and we sat around him as though birds were upon our heads, and he had a stick with which he was scratching the ground. He raised his head and said: "Seek refuge with Allah from the punishment of the grave," twice or thrice. In the hadith of Jarir he added here: And he said: "Indeed he hears the sound of their sandals when they turn away, when it is said to him: O so-and-so, who is your Lord? What is your religion? Who is your Prophet? ..." The hadith.]], and you also believe that the grave is either a garden from the gardens of Paradise or a pit from the pits of the Fire[[Recorded by al-Tabarani in al-Awsat (8613) with his chain from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The grave is either a garden from the gardens of Paradise or a pit from the pits of the Fire."]]; i.e., in it is either punishment or reward. And you also believe in Paradise and Hell, and everything related to the Last Day falls within our saying: to believe in Allah and the Last Day.

Qadar: the decree of Allah, Mighty and Majestic; meaning you must believe that Allah has decreed everything. That is because "Allah created the Pen and said to it: Write. It said: What shall I write? He said: Write what will exist until the Day of Resurrection"[[Recorded by al-Tirmidhi (2155) from the hadith of 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit, may Allah be pleased with him, and its wording: "The first thing Allah created was the Pen, and He said: Write. It said: What shall I write? He said: Write the decree of what has been and what will be until eternity."]]. So at that very hour, what will exist until the Day of Resurrection was run according to the decree.

Thus, faith in His saying ﴿except those who believed﴾ includes what? Faith in the six foundations that the Messenger (ﷺ) explained.

As for His saying ﴿and did righteous deeds﴾, its meaning is that they performed righteous deeds: prayer, zakat, fasting, pilgrimage, kindness to parents, maintaining ties of kinship, and other things. They did not limit themselves to what is in the heart alone, but acted and produced.

Righteous deeds are those that comprise two things: the first is sincerity to Allah, and the second is following the Messenger (ﷺ). That is because if a deed is not sincere to Allah, it is rejected. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said in the sacred hadith which the Prophet (ﷺ) narrates from Him: Allah said: "I am the most self-sufficient of partners in need of partners. Whoever does a deed in which he associates others with Me, I abandon him and his associate"[[Recorded by Muslim (2985/46) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him.]]. So if you stand to pray to be seen by people, or give charity to be seen by people, or seek knowledge to be seen by people, or maintain ties of kinship to be seen by people, or other such things, the deed is rejected even if it is righteous in its outward appearance.

Likewise following: if you do a deed that the Messenger (ﷺ) did not do and you draw near to Allah by it, even with sincerity to Allah, it will not be accepted from you; because the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever does a deed that is not in accordance with our command, it is rejected"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2697) in similar wording, and Muslim (1718/18), the wording of the latter, from the hadith of 'A'isha, may Allah be pleased with her.]].

So a righteous deed is one that combines two qualities: the first is sincerity to Allah, and the second is what? Following the Messenger (ﷺ).

﴿and advised one another to truth﴾: i.e., some of them would advise others with the truth, and the truth is the Sharia; meaning each of them advises the other: if he sees him neglecting an obligation, he advises him; he says: O my brother, benefit yourself, perform the obligation. If he sees him committing a prohibited act, he advises him; he says: O my brother, avoid what is forbidden. They did not limit themselves to benefiting themselves, but benefited themselves and others. ﴿advised one another to truth﴾: the truth here means what? The Sharia; they advise one another to it.

﴿and advised one another to patience﴾. Patience is restraining the self from what should not be done. The scholars divided it into three categories, saying: patience is patience in obedience to Allah, patience in refraining from what Allah has forbidden, and patience with the decrees of Allah; three categories.

Patience in obedience: many people feel laziness about praying in congregation, for example; they do not go to the mosque, saying: I pray at home and have fulfilled the obligation, so they become lazy. We say: O my brother, be patient with yourself, restrain it, compel it to pray in congregation.

Many people, when they see the zakat on their wealth is large, become stingy and miserly and begin to waver: shall I pay out this large amount, or leave it, or later on? And the like. We say: O my brother, be patient with yourself, compel it to pay zakat.

And likewise the rest of the acts of worship, for acts of worship, as Allah said about prayer: ﴿And indeed it is heavy except for the humble﴾ [al-Baqarah 45]. You will find that most of Allah's servants find acts of worship burdensome, so they advise one another to patience: be patient in obedience, do not tire, do not be lazy.

Likewise patience in refraining from sin: some people are driven by their souls toward forbidden earnings, whether through usury, or through cheating and lying, or through deception, or other kinds of what is forbidden. So we say: be patient, O my brother, be patient with yourself, do not deal in a forbidden manner.

Some people are also afflicted with looking at women; you find him walking in the market, and whenever a woman passes he follows her with his gaze. We say: O my brother, be patient, restrain yourself from this thing.

Patience with the decrees of Allah: a person is afflicted with sickness in his body; a person is afflicted with the loss of some of his wealth; a person is afflicted with the loss of his loved ones, and he grows distressed, becomes resentful, and suffers pain. So they advise one another: be patient, O my brother, this is a matter decreed; distress does not benefit anything, and continued grief does not lift grief; be patient, consider that this thing never existed at all. For example, a person who lost a million riyals grieved over it and was tormented by it; what do we say to him? We say: be patient, O my brother, consider that this million was never there. Did you not come out of your mother's womb with no clothes on?! Consider that this never was.

Likewise children. For example, a person tested by the death of his son; we say: O my brother, be patient, consider that this son was never created. Then, as the Messenger (ﷺ) said to one of his daughters: "Tell her to be patient and seek reward; for to Allah belongs what He takes and to Him belongs what He gives"[[Recorded by al-Bukhari (7448) and Muslim (923/11), the wording of the latter, with their two chains, from Usamah ibn Zayd, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: We were with the Prophet (ﷺ) when one of his daughters sent for him, informing him that a child of hers, a son, was dying. He said to the messenger: "Return to her and inform her that to Allah belongs what He takes and to Him belongs what He gives, and everything with Him has an appointed term. So tell her to be patient and seek reward ..." The hadith.]]. The whole matter belongs to Allah, not to you. So when Allah, Exalted, takes back what is His, how can you blame your Lord?! How can you be resentful?!

These, then, are the types of patience: the first is patience in obeying Allah, the second is refraining from disobeying Allah, and the third is patience with the decrees of Allah.

Which of them is hardest on the souls? This varies. Some people find performing acts of obedience very difficult and burdensome; and some people, on the contrary, find obedience easy, but abstaining from sin is hard and arduous for them, a great hardship. And some people find it easy to be patient in obedience and patient in refraining from sin, but cannot bear patience in calamities; they are unable, to the point that their state may lead them to apostasy — and we seek refuge with Allah — as Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿And among the people is he who worships Allah on an edge; if good befalls him, he is reassured by it, but if a trial befalls him, he turns back on his face; he has lost this world and the Hereafter. That is the clear loss﴾ [al-Hajj 11].

Therefore, from this verse we take that Allah, glorified and exalted, emphasized with an oath, reinforced by "inna" and the lam, that all of the children of Adam are what? Losers. Indeed, they are in loss; loss encompasses them from every side, except for those who possess these four qualities: faith (iman), righteous deeds, mutual exhortation to truth, and mutual exhortation to patience.

Al-Shafi'i (may Allah have mercy on him) said: "If Allah had sent down no proof to His servants except this surah, it would have been sufficient for them." That is, it would have sufficed them as admonition, not as legislation, because there is nothing in it of legislation: there is no purification, no prayer, no zakat, no hajj, and no fasting in it. But it suffices them as admonition. Every sensible person knows that he is in loss unless he possesses these four qualities, and so he will strive, to the extent he is able, to acquire these four qualities.

We ask Allah to make us and you among the winners who are granted success.

Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and may Allah send blessings and peace upon our Prophet Muhammad, and upon his family and companions, and those who follow them in goodness until the Day of Judgment.

If he sees him committing a prohibited act, he advises him; he says: O my brother, avoid what is forbidden. They did not limit themselves to benefiting themselves, but benefited themselves and others. ﴿advised one another to truth﴾: the truth here means what? The Sharia; they advise one another to it.

﴿and advised one another to patience﴾. Patience is restraining the self from what should not be done. The scholars divided it into three categories, saying: patience is patience in obedience to Allah, patience in refraining from what Allah has forbidden, and patience with the decrees of Allah; three categories.

Patience in obedience: many people feel laziness about praying in congregation, for example; they do not go to the mosque, saying: I pray at home and have fulfilled the obligation, so they become lazy. We say: O my brother, be patient with yourself, restrain it, compel it to pray in congregation.

Many people, when they see the zakat on their wealth is large, become stingy and miserly and begin to waver: shall I pay out this large amount, or leave it, or later on? And the like. We say: O my brother, be patient with yourself, compel it to pay zakat.

And likewise the rest of the acts of worship, for acts of worship, as Allah said about prayer: ﴿And indeed it is heavy except for the humble﴾ [al-Baqarah 45]. You will find that most of Allah's servants find acts of worship burdensome, so they advise one another to patience: be patient in obedience, do not tire, do not be lazy.

Likewise patience in refraining from sin: some people are driven by their souls toward forbidden earnings, whether through usury, or through cheating and lying, or through deception, or other kinds of what is forbidden. So we say: be patient, O my brother, be patient with yourself, do not deal in a forbidden manner.

Some people are also afflicted with looking at women; you find him walking in the market, and whenever a woman passes he follows her with his gaze. We say: O my brother, be patient, restrain yourself from this thing.

Patience with the decrees of Allah: a person is afflicted with sickness in his body; a person is afflicted with the loss of some of his wealth; a person is afflicted with the loss of his loved ones, and he grows distressed, becomes resentful, and suffers pain. So they advise one another: be patient, O my brother, this is a matter decreed; distress does not benefit anything, and continued grief does not lift grief; be patient, consider that this thing never existed at all. For example, a person who lost a million riyals grieved over it and was tormented by it; what do we say to him? We say: be patient, O my brother, consider that this million was never there. Did you not come out of your mother's womb with no clothes on?! Consider that this never was.

Likewise children. For example, a person tested by the death of his son; we say: O my brother, be patient, consider that this son was never created. Then, as the Messenger (ﷺ) said to one of his daughters: "Tell her to be patient and seek reward; for to Allah belongs what He takes and to Him belongs what He gives"[[Recorded by al-Bukhari (7448) and Muslim (923/11), the wording of the latter, with their two chains, from Usamah ibn Zayd, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: We were with the Prophet (ﷺ) when one of his daughters sent for him, informing him that a child of hers, a son, was dying. He said to the messenger: "Return to her and inform her that to Allah belongs what He takes and to Him belongs what He gives, and everything with Him has an appointed term. So tell her to be patient and seek reward ..." The hadith.]]. The whole matter belongs to Allah, not to you. So when Allah, Exalted, takes back what is His, how can you blame your Lord?! How can you be resentful?!

These, then, are the types of patience: the first is patience in obeying Allah, the second is refraining from disobeying Allah, and the third is patience with the decrees of Allah.

Which of them is hardest on the souls? This varies. Some people find performing acts of obedience very difficult and burdensome; and some people, on the contrary, find obedience easy, but abstaining from sin is hard and arduous for them, a great hardship. And some people find it easy to be patient in obedience and patient in refraining from sin, but cannot bear patience in calamities; they are unable, to the point that their state may lead them to apostasy — and we seek refuge with Allah — as Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿And among the people is he who worships Allah on an edge; if good befalls him, he is reassured by it, but if a trial befalls him, he turns back on his face; he has lost this world and the Hereafter. That is the clear loss﴾ [al-Hajj 11].

Therefore, from this verse we take that Allah, glorified and exalted, emphasized with an oath, reinforced by "inna" and the lam, that all of the children of Adam are what? Losers. Indeed, they are in loss; loss encompasses them from every side, except for those who possess these four qualities: faith (iman), righteous deeds, mutual exhortation to truth, and mutual exhortation to patience.

Al-Shafi'i (may Allah have mercy on him) said: "If Allah had sent down no proof to His servants except this surah, it would have been sufficient for them." That is, it would have sufficed them as admonition, not as legislation, because there is nothing in it of legislation: there is no purification, no prayer, no zakat, no hajj, and no fasting in it. But it suffices them as admonition. Every sensible person knows that he is in loss unless he possesses these four qualities, and so he will strive, to the extent he is able, to acquire these four qualities.

We ask Allah to make us and you among the winners who are granted success.

Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and may Allah send blessings and peace upon our Prophet Muhammad, and upon his family and companions, and those who follow them in goodness until the Day of Judgment.

To proceed: this is the weekly session called the "Open Door" meeting, and it is the ninety-ninth. This session takes place on Thursday, the fourteenth of Rabi' al-Awwal in the year one thousand four hundred and sixteen (AH), and in it we speak, by the will of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, about the tafsir of Surat al-'Asr.

Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿By time, indeed mankind is in loss﴾ [al-'Asr 1-2]. So what is meant by al-'Asr?

It has been said: the intended meaning of al-'Asr is the end of the day, because the end of the day is its best part; and the 'Asr prayer is called the middle prayer (al-Salat al-Wusta), i.e., the most excellent (al-Fudla), as the Prophet (ﷺ) named it.

And it has been said: al-'Asr is time itself. This is the more correct view: al-'Asr is time, which Allah swore by because of what occurs within it of changing circumstances, shifting affairs, and the alternation of days among people, and other things that are witnessed in the present and reported about in the past. So al-'Asr is the time in which creation lives, and its periods vary in hardship and ease, war and peace, health and sickness, righteous deeds and evil deeds, and other things that are known to all.

On what did Allah swear? On His saying: ﴿indeed mankind is in loss﴾. The word "mankind" (al-Insan) here is general, because the intended meaning is the genus. The sign of a noun intended in a general sense is that the word "kull" (all) can take its place, i.e., in place of (al-, the definite article). So here, if it were said, "Every human is in loss," that would be the meaning.

The meaning of the noble verse is that Allah swore an oath concerning the condition of mankind, that they are in loss, i.e., in ruin and deficiency in all their circumstances, in this world and in the Hereafter, except for those whom Allah, Mighty and Majestic, excepts. And this sentence, as you see, is emphasized with three emphases: the first is the oath; the second is "inna"; the third is the lam. And He used the phrase ﴿in loss﴾ so that it would be more emphatic than saying "losers" (lakhasir). That is because "fi" (in) — what does it mean? It means enclosure, so it is as if the human being is immersed in loss, and loss surrounds him from every side.

﴿Except those who believed and did righteous deeds and advised one another to truth and advised one another to patience﴾ [al-'Asr 3]. Allah, glorified and exalted, excepted those who possess these four attributes. The first attribute: faith that is not mixed with doubt or hesitation. In what? In what the Messenger (ﷺ) explained when Jibril asked him about faith; he said: "That you believe in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Last Day, and that you believe in divine decree, its good and its evil."[[Recorded by Muslim (8/1) from the hadith of Ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both.]] The explanation of this hadith would be lengthy if we discussed it now, but we have discussed it in many places. Those who believe in these six foundations are the believers, but it must be a faith with no doubt or hesitation; meaning that you believe in these things as though you see them with your own eyes.

People in this regard are of three categories:
The first category: a believer who is sincere, with faith that has no doubt or hesitation in it.
The second category: a disbelieving, denying rejecter.
The third category: the wavering one.

So who is saved from these three categories? The saved one is the first category, who believes with faith free of hesitation: he believes in Allah — in His existence, His names, His attributes, His divinity and His lordship, and other things known of the attributes of the Lord, Majestic and Exalted. He believes in the angels, who are an unseen world, whom Allah created from light, and assigned to tasks, some of which are known and some of which are not known. Jibril, peace be upon him, is charged with revelation, which he brings down from Allah to the prophets and messengers; Mikail is charged with rain and plants — i.e., Allah entrusted him with rain and all that relates to rain, and with plants; Israfil is charged with blowing the Trumpet; Malik is charged with the Fire; Ridwan is charged with Paradise. Among the angels are those whose names we do not know and whose tasks we also do not know. But it has come in a hadith from the Prophet (ﷺ) that "there is no spot of four fingers' breadth in the heavens except that there is an angel standing for Allah, or bowing, or prostrating"[[Recorded by al-Tirmidhi (2312) from the hadith of Abu Dharr, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I see what you do not see and hear what you do not hear. The heaven has creaked, and it has the right to creak; there is no spot of four fingers in it except that an angel is placing his forehead in prostration to Allah. By Allah, if you knew what I know, you would laugh little and weep much, and you would not enjoy women on beds, and you would go out to the high ground supplicating to Allah." I wish I had been a tree that is cut down. The phrase "I wish I had been a tree that is cut down" is the words of Abu Dharr, may Allah be pleased with him; see Musnad Ahmad (21516).]].

Likewise we believe in the books that Allah sent down to the messengers, peace be upon them, and we believe in the messengers. Those whom Allah has related to us, we believe in them by their individual identities; and those whom He has not related to us, we believe in them in general, because Allah has not related to us all the accounts of the messengers. Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿Among them are those We have related to you, and among them are those We have not related to you﴾ [Ghafir 78].

The Last Day is the Day of Resurrection, the day when people come out of their graves for recompense, "barefoot, naked, uncircumcised, and destitute"[[Recorded by al-Bukhari (3349) and Muslim (2860/58), the wording of the latter, with their two chains, from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood among us giving a sermon and said: "O people, you will be gathered to Allah barefoot, naked, uncircumcised: ﴿As We began the first creation, We will repeat it; a promise upon Us; indeed We are ever doing﴾ [al-Anbiya' 104] ..." The hadith. As for the word "destitute" (buhman), it came in what Ahmad (16042) recorded from the hadith of 'Abdullah ibn Unays, may Allah be pleased with him, in which it says: "People will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection — or he said: the servants — naked, uncircumcised, destitute."]]. "Barefoot" means those who have no sandals or shoes, i.e., their feet are bare; "naked" means those who have no clothes; "uncircumcised" means those who have not been circumcised; and "destitute" means those who have no wealth. They will be gathered in this state. "When the Prophet (ﷺ) mentioned that they would be naked, 'A'isha said: O Messenger of Allah, do men and women look at one another?! He said: 'The matter is greater than that'"[[Recorded by al-Bukhari (6527) and Muslim (2859/56), the wording of the latter, with their two chains, to 'A'isha who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "People will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection barefoot, naked, uncircumcised." I said: O Messenger of Allah, do men and women look at one another all together? He (ﷺ) said: "O 'A'isha, the matter is more severe than that they look at one another." As for the word "destitute" (buhman), it came in what Ahmad (16042) recorded from the hadith of 'Abdullah ibn Unays, may Allah be pleased with him, in which it says: "People will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection — or he said: the servants — naked, uncircumcised, destitute."]]; i.e., the matter is too great for them to look at one another, because each person is preoccupied with himself.

Shaykh al-Islam, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Among faith in the Last Day is belief in everything the Prophet (ﷺ) informed about that will occur after death. So it is obligatory to believe in the trial of the grave, i.e., the testing that the deceased undergoes when he is buried and his companions have turned away from him; two angels come to him and ask him about his Lord, his religion, and his Prophet[[Recorded by Abu Dawud (4753) with his chain from al-Bara' ibn 'Azib who said: We went out with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to the funeral of a man from the Ansar, and we reached the grave before it had been dug in its niche. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sat down and we sat around him as though birds were upon our heads, and he had a stick with which he was scratching the ground. He raised his head and said: "Seek refuge with Allah from the punishment of the grave," twice or thrice. In the hadith of Jarir he added here: And he said: "Indeed he hears the sound of their sandals when they turn away, when it is said to him: O so-and-so, who is your Lord? What is your religion? Who is your Prophet? ..." The hadith.]], and you also believe that the grave is either a garden from the gardens of Paradise or a pit from the pits of the Fire[[Recorded by al-Tabarani in al-Awsat (8613) with his chain from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The grave is either a garden from the gardens of Paradise or a pit from the pits of the Fire."]]; i.e., in it is either punishment or reward. And you also believe in Paradise and Hell, and everything related to the Last Day falls within our saying: to believe in Allah and the Last Day.

Qadar: the decree of Allah, Mighty and Majestic; meaning you must believe that Allah has decreed everything. That is because "Allah created the Pen and said to it: Write. It said: What shall I write? He said: Write what will exist until the Day of Resurrection"[[Recorded by al-Tirmidhi (2155) from the hadith of 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit, may Allah be pleased with him, and its wording: "The first thing Allah created was the Pen, and He said: Write. It said: What shall I write? He said: Write the decree of what has been and what will be until eternity."]]. So at that very hour, what will exist until the Day of Resurrection was run according to the decree.

Thus, faith in His saying ﴿except those who believed﴾ includes what? Faith in the six foundations that the Messenger (ﷺ) explained.

As for His saying ﴿and did righteous deeds﴾, its meaning is that they performed righteous deeds: prayer, zakat, fasting, pilgrimage, kindness to parents, maintaining ties of kinship, and other things. They did not limit themselves to what is in the heart alone, but acted and produced.

Righteous deeds are those that comprise two things: the first is sincerity to Allah, and the second is following the Messenger (ﷺ). That is because if a deed is not sincere to Allah, it is rejected. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said in the sacred hadith which the Prophet (ﷺ) narrates from Him: Allah said: "I am the most self-sufficient of partners in need of partners. Whoever does a deed in which he associates others with Me, I abandon him and his associate"[[Recorded by Muslim (2985/46) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him.]]. So if you stand to pray to be seen by people, or give charity to be seen by people, or seek knowledge to be seen by people, or maintain ties of kinship to be seen by people, or other such things, the deed is rejected even if it is righteous in its outward appearance.

Likewise following: if you do a deed that the Messenger (ﷺ) did not do and you draw near to Allah by it, even with sincerity to Allah, it will not be accepted from you; because the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever does a deed that is not in accordance with our command, it is rejected"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2697) in similar wording, and Muslim (1718/18), the wording of the latter, from the hadith of 'A'isha, may Allah be pleased with her.]].

So a righteous deed is one that combines two qualities: the first is sincerity to Allah, and the second is what? Following the Messenger (ﷺ).

﴿and advised one another to truth﴾: i.e., some of them would advise others with the truth, and the truth is the Sharia; meaning each of them advises the other: if he sees him neglecting an obligation, he advises him; he says: O my brother, benefit yourself, perform the obligation. If he sees him committing a prohibited act, he advises him; he says: O my brother, avoid what is forbidden. They did not limit themselves to benefiting themselves, but benefited themselves and others. ﴿advised one another to truth﴾: the truth here means what? The Sharia; they advise one another to it.

﴿and advised one another to patience﴾. Patience is restraining the self from what should not be done. The scholars divided it into three categories, saying: patience is patience in obedience to Allah, patience in refraining from what Allah has forbidden, and patience with the decrees of Allah; three categories.

Patience in obedience: many people feel laziness about praying in congregation, for example; they do not go to the mosque, saying: I pray at home and have fulfilled the obligation, so they become lazy. We say: O my brother, be patient with yourself, restrain it, compel it to pray in congregation.

Many people, when they see the zakat on their wealth is large, become stingy and miserly and begin to waver: shall I pay out this large amount, or leave it, or later on? And the like. We say: O my brother, be patient with yourself, compel it to pay zakat.

And likewise the rest of the acts of worship, for acts of worship, as Allah said about prayer: ﴿And indeed it is heavy except for the humble﴾ [al-Baqarah 45]. You will find that most of Allah's servants find acts of worship burdensome, so they advise one another to patience: be patient in obedience, do not tire, do not be lazy.

Likewise patience in refraining from sin: some people are driven by their souls toward forbidden earnings, whether through usury, or through cheating and lying, or through deception, or other kinds of what is forbidden. So we say: be patient, O my brother, be patient with yourself, do not deal in a forbidden manner.

Some people are also afflicted with looking at women; you find him walking in the market, and whenever a woman passes he follows her with his gaze. We say: O my brother, be patient, restrain yourself from this thing.

Patience with the decrees of Allah: a person is afflicted with sickness in his body; a person is afflicted with the loss of some of his wealth; a person is afflicted with the loss of his loved ones, and he grows distressed, becomes resentful, and suffers pain. So they advise one another: be patient, O my brother, this is a matter decreed; distress does not benefit anything, and continued grief does not lift grief; be patient, consider that this thing never existed at all. For example, a person who lost a million riyals grieved over it and was tormented by it; what do we say to him? We say: be patient, O my brother, consider that this million was never there. Did you not come out of your mother's womb with no clothes on?! Consider that this never was.

Likewise children. For example, a person tested by the death of his son; we say: O my brother, be patient, consider that this son was never created. Then, as the Messenger (ﷺ) said to one of his daughters: "Tell her to be patient and seek reward; for to Allah belongs what He takes and to Him belongs what He gives"[[Recorded by al-Bukhari (7448) and Muslim (923/11), the wording of the latter, with their two chains, from Usamah ibn Zayd, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: We were with the Prophet (ﷺ) when one of his daughters sent for him, informing him that a child of hers, a son, was dying. He said to the messenger: "Return to her and inform her that to Allah belongs what He takes and to Him belongs what He gives, and everything with Him has an appointed term. So tell her to be patient and seek reward ..." The hadith.]]. The whole matter belongs to Allah, not to you. So when Allah, Exalted, takes back what is His, how can you blame your Lord?! How can you be resentful?!

These, then, are the types of patience: the first is patience in obeying Allah, the second is refraining from disobeying Allah, and the third is patience with the decrees of Allah.

Which of them is hardest on the souls? This varies. Some people find performing acts of obedience very difficult and burdensome; and some people, on the contrary, find obedience easy, but abstaining from sin is hard and arduous for them, a great hardship. And some people find it easy to be patient in obedience and patient in refraining from sin, but cannot bear patience in calamities; they are unable, to the point that their state may lead them to apostasy — and we seek refuge with Allah — as Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿And among the people is he who worships Allah on an edge; if good befalls him, he is reassured by it, but if a trial befalls him, he turns back on his face; he has lost this world and the Hereafter. That is the clear loss﴾ [al-Hajj 11].

Therefore, from this verse we take that Allah, glorified and exalted, emphasized with an oath, reinforced by "inna" and the lam, that all of the children of Adam are what? Losers. Indeed, they are in loss; loss encompasses them from every side, except for those who possess these four qualities: faith (iman), righteous deeds, mutual exhortation to truth, and mutual exhortation to patience.

Al-Shafi'i (may Allah have mercy on him) said: "If Allah had sent down no proof to His servants except this surah, it would have been sufficient for them." That is, it would have sufficed them as admonition, not as legislation, because there is nothing in it of legislation: there is no purification, no prayer, no zakat, no hajj, and no fasting in it. But it suffices them as admonition. Every sensible person knows that he is in loss unless he possesses these four qualities, and so he will strive, to the extent he is able, to acquire these four qualities.

We ask Allah to make us and you among the winners who are granted success.
